drivers.title: OPEC+ output nears pre-war levels and IEA sees Q4 surplus; oil heads for second weekly loss
drivers.rationale: Gulf producers have restored output around Hormuz and the IEA projects a surplus -> the remaining war premium in Brent near $96 erodes -> producers lag and airlines gain. Brent is already -12.8% in 20 days and mine incidents persist, so the size is moderate.

drivers.title: US proposes new 'overcapacity' tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU, India and Brazil; partners vow to hit back
drivers.rationale: New subsidy-based tariffs explicitly aimed at China's overcapacity, plus Chinese retaliation threats and the Huawei conviction -> escalation risk after the summit truce -> Apple, Nike and China ETFs lag US steelmakers. FXI is only +0.6% on the week, so this is not priced.

drivers.title: US and China discuss tariffs and farm trade ahead of Xi-Trump meeting; Trump, Putin and Xi to meet in China next week
drivers.rationale: A leaders' summit with tariffs and farm purchases on the agenda, after China extended its tariff truce -> lower odds of new escalation and scope for a deliverable -> China ETFs, Apple and Nike gain relative to steelmakers. FXI fell 4.2% this week, so a deal is not priced. The chip-curb push in Congress is the main risk.

drivers.title: Attacks on Hormuz shipping hit wartime highs; Houthis threaten Jeddah and hit a Saudi refinery; Iranian drone kills two in Kuwait
drivers.rationale: Hormuz attacks are at wartime highs, the blockade looks set to persist (end-by-year odds 14%) and the Houthis now threaten Saudi Red Sea ports, the main Hormuz bypass -> two chokepoints at risk -> freight and insurance rates stay high -> shippers beat transport users. BOAT is still -9.5% in 20 days, so this is not priced.

drivers.title: Houthis gain ground at Bab al-Mandab and threaten Saudi Red Sea ports
drivers.rationale: Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandab shoreline and threats to Saudi Red Sea ports such as Yanbu, the main bypass for Hormuz -> a second chokepoint at risk alongside Hormuz -> higher freight and insurance rates help shippers and hurt transport users. BOAT fell 5% in the sell-off, so this is not priced, but the threats may not be carried out.

drivers.title: Iran war grinds on with tanker mines, Gulf strikes and a third US carrier, but ceasefire odds rise as Trump calls new strikes unlikely
drivers.rationale: Headlines stress attacks, but the money points the other way: US-Iran ceasefire odds rose 10-12 points (56% by 30 Nov, 84% by year-end) and Brent fell again -> the escalation premium keeps fading -> energy majors lag airlines. Mine incidents persist and a risk-off market hurts airlines, so confidence is low.

drivers.title: Spain's Hernández de Cos set to lead the ECB as Simkus says a December hike may not be enough
drivers.rationale: A December hike looks expected and hawks are arguing for more, with energy-driven inflation -> higher euro-area yields -> European banks beat real estate and utilities. A mainstream incoming president limits the hawkish tail.

drivers.title: Spanish general election: PP favoured to win most seats, Feijóo 88% to be next PM
drivers.rationale: A PP-led government has opposed the Sánchez-era bank levy -> better odds of easing it -> domestic Spanish banks like CaixaBank benefit. At 88% the outcome is mostly priced, so the size is small.

drivers.title: Bundesbank's Nagel backs a December ECB hike; BoE expected to hike, RBA hikes again
drivers.rationale: A broadening hawkish chorus locks in the December hike -> euro yields supported -> banks over real estate. Falling oil weakens the inflation case, so the size is small.

drivers.title: Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervention; US blacklists Megaspeed as Nvidia halts server shipments to Southeast Asia

A Democratic Congress is scrutinising the reinstatement -> enforcement is tightening in practice even as Bessent rules out new rules -> pressure on China-exposed chip and tool makers. White House support for Nvidia is the main offset.

drivers.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; Congress pushes China chip curbs as Bessent blames Lutnick for export-control lapses
drivers.rationale: The spy scandal, an H200 diversion to a blacklisted university and a cabinet row over lax enforcement give a Democratic Congress cover for China chip bills -> tighter enforcement and entity listings -> pressure on Nvidia and chip-tool makers with China exposure. The Xi summit next week could produce a softer White House line, so confidence is moderate.
